extracted.intended_audience: John Jay, James Madison, the Count de Moustier — American statesmen, diplomatic correspondents, and readers of Jefferson's correspondence
extracted.subtask_description: Transcriptions of Thomas Jefferson's May 1788 letters to American political figures (John Jay, James Madison, Count de Moustier) addressing national credit, public finance, diplomacy, constitutional structure, and judicial reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of good national credit
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Possessing a good credit I consider as indispensable, in the present system of carrying on war.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson argues national credit is essential because war requires expenditures beyond annual resources; possessing good credit allows command of funds quickly on foreign exchanges. He recommends cultivating credit 'with the utmost attention' and to use it sparingly even when possessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When borrowing, appropriate taxes to pay interest
rubrics_metrics.description: 'They never borrow, without establishing taxes for the payment of the interest, and they never yet failed one day in that payment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses England as the exemplar: to obtain and retain high credit, any loan must be accompanied by a dedicated revenue source for interest so payments are punctual. This discipline underpins market confidence and better borrowing terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: First acts of a new government should secure credit by consolidating and funding European debts
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The first act of the new government should be some operation, whereby they may assume to themselves this station... Digest the whole, public and private, Dutch, French, and Spanish, into a table...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps Jefferson prescribes: compile schedules of interest and principal due, select a most-certain revenue to pay interest and provide prospect for principal, apply surpluses to buy paper on Amsterdam exchange, open a loan in Holland to fund and consolidate debts, and publish payments honestly and annually to inspire confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent, honest annual publication of payments
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Honest and annual publications of the payments made, will inspire confidence, while silence would conceal nothing from those interested to know.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular public accounting of debt servicing is recommended as a credibility-building measure; concealment undermines trust and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate payment of arrears to foreign creditors (French officers)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I must beg you to press on the treasury board; that is, an immediate order for the payment of the three years’ arrearages to the French officers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpaid arrears produce ill humor among influential creditors and can damage diplomatic and financial standing; Jefferson urges prompt settlement to avert 'desperate measures' and calm agitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use of credit even when obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: 'My wish would be, to possess it in the highest degree, but to use it little.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson counsels prudent fiscal behavior: secure credit for security and flexibility, but avoid its routine use to prevent vulnerability to better-capitalized rivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution should include a declaration of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: 'There are two things... 1. The want of a declaration of rights. I am in hopes the opposition in Virginia will remedy this, and produce such a declaration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson views an explicit bill/declaration of rights as an essential constitutional safeguard that should be added if absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perpetual re-eligibility of the President
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The perpetual re-eligibility of the President... I fear, will make that an office for life, first, and then hereditary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson warns that unlimited re-eligibility risks creating a de facto lifelong or hereditary executive; he treats limits on tenure as necessary to prevent monarchical tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed representative structure: two houses (Commons and Nobles)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The best seems to me, that of dividing them into two Houses, of Commons and Nobles; the Commons to be chosen by the Provincial Assemblies... and the Nobles by the body of Noblesse, as in Scotland.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson presents this as one viable scheme for structuring representation at a States-General, while acknowledging many projects exist and no single scheme is certain to be preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal justice reforms (abolish torture; allow counsel; specify offences; respite executions)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'By these ordinances, 1. The criminal law is reformed, by abolishing examination on the sellette... by substituting an oath, instead of torture... by allowing counsel to the prisoner for his defence; obliging the judges to specify in their judgments the offence for which he is condemned; and respiting execution a month, except in the case of sedition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson endorses these measures as improvements and as evidence the monarchy is late in yielding to philanthropic progress. He views them as legitimate exercises of legislative power and as civilizing reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganize judiciary to reduce parliaments' jurisdiction and limit special courts
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The organization of the whole judiciary department is changed, by the institution of subordinate jurisdictions, the taking from the parliaments the cognizance of all causes of less value than twenty thousand livres, reducing their numbers... and suppressing a number of special courts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson sees this reorganization as potentially beneficial in principle but warns it may concentrate power in the crown unless remedied by representative composition of appellate bodies (Plenary court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of high courts should be representative, not royal favorites
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The right of registering the laws is taken from the parliaments, and transferred to a Plenary court... a great proportion of them are from descriptions of men always candidates for the royal favor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson criticizes creating life-tenured courts filled by royal dependents; he suggests making such courts representative (e.g., members sent from Provincial Assemblies) to preserve legitimacy and avoid concentration of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic handling of captives and ransom negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I had taken measures to have it believed at Algiers, that our government withdrew its attention from our captives there. This was to prepare their captors for the ransoming them at a reasonable price.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical misinformation can be used to obtain more favorable ransom terms; Jefferson advises restraint in communicating government views to avoid inflating demands, and to act only when funds permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms for allowing nationals to serve in foreign navies (Paul Jones case)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'She insures to him the rank of rear-admiral; will give him a separate command... he has made it a condition, that he shall be free at all times to return to the orders of Congress... and also, that he shall not, in any case be expected to bear arms against France.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When American officers accept foreign employment, Jefferson insists on contractual protections: freedom to return to national orders and limits on fighting particular allies; recognition (rank) at home is suggested as reward and to improve future usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade/port regulation — preserve valuable navigation/entrepôt rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (paraphrase) 'Preserve valuable articles relative to our ships; abandon less useful entrepôt privileges (codfish) but avoid unintended exclusions such as whale-oil.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson negotiated to save valuable commercial privileges and cautions that clerical errors can unintentionally harm trade (whale-oil exclusion), which should be corrected promptly to protect export interests.
